newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST-Fortis 9-month net profit seen up 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Fortis 9-month net profit seen up 17 pct.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis is expected to announce a net profit rise of just over 17 percent for the first nine months of 1996 to 549 million ECU on Thursday, Dutch analysts said.
But Fortis would not be able to repeat the substantial first half profit growth in banking, they said.
"The increase for the banking sector is smoothing out," said analyst Tom Muller of NIBStrating.
The first half profit increase of 21 percent to 366 million European currency units (ECU) was mainly driven by the group's banking business.
Banking profits rose 27 percent to 258 million ECU during the first six months of 1996.
Ten analysts polled by Reuters said Fortis Amev, the Dutch parent company of Fortis, was expected to show an average rise in net profit of 15.3 percent to 598 million guilders.
Fortis Amev and Belgium's Fortis AG are the joint owners of Fortis.

Daan Worm of ING Barings, noting that Fortis results differed greatly from quarter to quarter because of capital gains and exceptional items, said profits over the first nine months would rise by just over 12 percent to 526 million ECU.
He added that in the final quarter of the year, the Dutch-Belgian firm would make up for the slow-down in growth.
For the whole of 1996, he forecasts a profit rise of 17 percent to 736 million ECU.
Analysts said the group was likely to show a moderate rise in the life insurance sector.
"Non-life, a relatively big sector for Fortis, should show an upswing in results," said Jeff Meys of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
All Dutch insurance firms have said the recent rise in premiums had made car insurance profitable again and, analysts said, this should be the case for Fortis.
They said health-insurance was also doing better, but they expected the biggest profit increase from this sector to occur during the last quarter of 1996.

The operating result on health insurance dipped to a loss of 23 million ECU in the last quarter of 1995, because of losses in Belgium and the U.S. "For the last three months of 1996 I foresee an operating profit of 15 million ECU for the group's health insurance operations," said Worm.
Analysts were upbeat on the acquisition of merchant bank Meespierson, which should be rounded off before the end of the year. -- Wendy Braanker, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
